Case Information: A 28-year-old man presented to the emergency department with a swollen and painful left ankle after landing awkwardly on his inverted left foot while playing basketball two hours earlier.
Physical Examination: The left ankle was markedly swollen and diffusely tender. He was unable to bear weight on the affected leg.
Diagnostic Tests: - Imaging Studies:    1. Radiographs of the left ankle showed no acute fracture or dislocation.    2. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a complete full-thickness tear of the anterior talofibular ligament with surrounding soft tissue edema; the posterior talofibular ligament was intact and no fracture line was identified.
Final Diagnosis: Complete tear of the anterior talofibular ligament (grade III lateral ankle sprain)
